content: The American Association for Laboratory Animal Science (AALAS) is a nonprofit organization established in 1950 to facilitate the exchange of knowledge and expertise in the care and use of laboratory animals. It has a membership base of approximately 12,000 individuals and organizations, including academic institutions, research facilities, government agencies, and commercial entities. The national headquarters is located in Memphis, Tennessee. National Meeting Since its inception in 1950, AALAS has hosted an annual National Meeting every fall. This five-day event includes workshops, lectures, poster presentations, and exhibits, catering to the diverse interests of its members. The meeting provides a platform for exhibitors to engage with professionals from academia, research institutions, government, and industry. Each year, eight professional and technical awards are presented to recognize excellence in laboratory animal science. The AALAS National Meeting is the largest global gathering of professionals dedicated to the care, use, and production of laboratory animals. Publications AALAS produces two peer-reviewed scientific journals and two newsletters to disseminate information and foster communication within the field of laboratory animal science. Comparative Medicine (CM): This bi-monthly international journal focuses on comparative and experimental medicine. It publishes scholarly articles on topics such as animal models, laboratory animal medicine, pathology, behavior, and biotechnology. The journal is indexed in Index Medicus and ranks in the top third of scientific journals according to the Science Citation Index. Dr. Linda Toth of Southern Illinois University School of Medicine serves as the editor-in-chief, with Dr. Ravi Tolwani of Rockefeller University as the associate editor. Journal of the American Association for Laboratory Animal Science (JAALAS): This bi-monthly journal serves as an official communication platform for AALAS. It includes peer-reviewed articles on animal biology, technology, facility operations, and compliance, as well as association news. The journal was previously known as Contemporary Topics in Laboratory Animal Science until 2006. Dr. Linda Toth is the editor-in-chief, and Dr. Susan Compton of Yale University serves as the associate editor. AALAS in Action: This bi-monthly newsletter is designed to enhance communication among AALAS members at both the national and branch levels. Its content is freely reproducible. Tech Talk: This bi-monthly publication focuses on the dissemination of professional information and technological advancements in laboratory animal science, promoting global knowledge-sharing in animal care methodologies. Certification Programs AALAS offers certification programs to validate technical knowledge and promote professionalism in laboratory animal science. Certified Manager of Animal Resources (CMAR): This certification is aimed at professionals in animal resources management. It requires passing four examinations, three of which are administered by the Institute for Certified Professional Managers (ICPM), and one by AALAS. Maintaining the CMAR designation involves annual recertification fees and continuing education credits. Technician Certification: AALAS certifies three levels of technician competence: Assistant Laboratory Animal Technician (ALAT), Laboratory Animal Technician (LAT), and Laboratory Animal Technologist (LATG). These certifications are widely recognized across various fields of laboratory animal care. Institute for Laboratory Animal Management (ILAM) The ILAM program provides specialized training in management concepts tailored to the laboratory animal science industry. It focuses on enhancing communication, team-building, and networking skills among professionals in leadership roles. The program addresses the growing complexity of managing laboratory animal facilities, emphasizing the need for administrative and technical expertise in addition to biological and veterinary training. AALAS Learning Library The AALAS Learning Library offers training courses for technicians, veterinarians, managers, IACUC members, and researchers working with animals in research or educational settings. These courses emphasize proper animal care and handling, help individuals prepare for AALAS certification, meet regulatory training requirements, and enhance technical knowledge. AALAS Foundation The AALAS Foundation is a nonprofit organization that funds initiatives to raise public awareness about biomedical research and its societal contributions. It provides outreach materials such as flyers, posters, videos, DVDs, and classroom resources to promote understanding of the importance of laboratory animal science.
